title: Reload+Reload: Exploiting Cache and Memory Contention Side Channel on AMD SEV
problem: AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) is designed to protect guest VMs in multi-tenant clouds via memory encryption, but two previously unknown side channels—cache flush timing and memory contention—expose information even through the SEV-SNP isolation boundary.
method: The authors discover and formalize two AMD-specific side channels: (1) a cache flush side channel exploitable via flush-set timing (RRFS), and (2) a memory contention side channel (RRMB). They construct two Reload+Reload attack variants that exploit these channels to observe memory access patterns without relying on the disabled Flush+Reload primitive. RRFS is used to build a covert channel for a Spectre attack; RRMB is used for AES-128 key extraction by timing memory block contention across VM boundaries under SEV-SNP.

title: GS-TG: 3D Gaussian Splatting Accelerator with Tile Grouping for Reducing Redundant Sorting while Preserving Rasterization Efficiency
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering faces a fundamental trade-off: large tile sizes reduce redundant sorting but increase unnecessary rasterization computations, limiting real-time performance in novel view synthesis.
method: GS-TG uses tile grouping during sorting to share operations across small tiles (creating virtual large tiles) while using bitmasks during rasterization to identify relevant small tiles. This enables sorting efficiency of large tiles with rasterization efficiency of small tiles, a lossless technique requiring no retraining.

title: Controlled Preemption: Amplifying Side-Channel Attacks from Userspace
problem: Many microarchitectural side-channel attacks are hampered by low temporal resolution measurements, which can preclude or significantly complicate extraction of sensitive information. Userspace attackers lack a mechanism to synchronize their observations with victim activity at fine-grained time resolution.
method: The paper introduces controlled preemption, a technique that allows a userspace attacker to precisely manipulate OS preemption timing in order to achieve fine-grained, synchronized measurement of victim microarchitectural state. By forcing preemption at attacker-chosen moments, the technique amplifies the signal quality of side-channel observations without requiring privileged access or hardware modifications.

title: SSpMV: A Sparsity-aware SpMV Framework Empowered by Multimodal Machine Learning
problem: Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication performance varies significantly across matrices and architectures; existing SpMV libraries use fixed algorithms that do not adapt to matrix sparsity patterns and hardware characteristics.
method: SSpMV integrates expert-designed features with multimodal neural network representations to predict the best-performing SpMV algorithm and parameters. MM-Adapter is a multimodal network capturing diverse computational feature modalities of SpMV (pattern, density, structure).

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference Efficiency through Block Dependency Analysis
problem: ML compilers perform data dependency analysis at element or operator granularity, which creates overly complex inter-operator dependencies that block efficient fusion and overlap, and obscures parallelizable computation opportunities, leaving significant GPU utilization on the table.
method: BlockDepend introduces a block-level dependency analysis framework in the ML compiler pipeline. By operating at the level of tile/block computations (below operator level but above scalar element level), it extracts simplified dependency relationships between operators and identifies previously hidden parallelizable computation pairs. These dependencies drive targeted inter-operator memory access optimizations (e.g., producer-consumer fusion, shared memory reuse) and expose additional kernel-level parallelism that can be scheduled concurrently on GPU compute units.

title: 13.6 A Via-Programmable DNN-Processor Fabrication Toward 1/40th Mask Cost
problem: Wearable AI-IoT devices require custom DNN accelerators, but each ASIC incurs substantial mask costs, making it economically infeasible to support diverse applications and architectures. The challenge is to reduce both fabrication cost and area overhead while supporting varied DNN topologies.
method: A via-programmable neuron array (VPNA) base chip is used with varied via placements to realize different DNN layers without changing photomasks. Two key techniques address implementation challenges: (1) Bit- and Neuron-Serial Circuit (BNSC) reduces programmable routing wire area by 1/1024, and (2) Sparse Binary Neural Networks (FS-NNN) reduce DNN size to fit on fewer VPNA tiles.

title: KVO-LLM: Boosting Long-Context Generation Throughput for Batched LLM Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference with batching incurs extreme external memory access (EMA) from KV cache; modern accelerators suffer PE under-utilization due to low arithmetic intensity, while existing KV compression trades accuracy for efficiency.
method: KVO-LLM combines algorithm-level KV optimization with architecture co-design: (1) algorithm: salient-token-aware quantization followed by attention-guided pruning of KV channels and tokens; (2) architecture: multi-core accelerator with operator fusion and cross-batch interleaving to maximize PE and DRAM bandwidth utilization.

title: CryptoBTB: A Secure Hierarchical BTB for Diverse Instruction Footprint Workloads
problem: Branch Target Buffer (BTB) timing attacks allow adversaries to infer victim BTB updates and mistrain branch predictors, bypassing privilege-level isolation and secure enclave protection; existing encrypted BTB schemes either have security weaknesses or encrypt the BTB index in-pipeline, exposing high latency.
method: CryptoBTB proposes a hierarchical exclusive BTB structure where the index encryption is decoupled from the BTB set index computation. The encryption step uses a low-latency scheme that obscures the set mapping without being on the critical prediction path; the hierarchical organization (L1 BTB + L2 BTB) avoids the collision-prone flat structure of prior work (HyBP), allowing the BTB capacity to be better utilized for workloads with large instruction footprints and reducing same-thread collisions.

title: Efficient Weight Mapping and Resource Scheduling on Crossbar-based Multi-core CIM Systems
problem: Multi-core crossbar-based CIM systems (eFlash-based SoCs) must optimize for both latency and resource utilization. Key compiler challenges include high parallel processing overhead, suboptimal resource utilization, and inefficient crossbar array assignment for CNNs, resulting in poor latency and low array utilization.
method: Proposes resource scheduling strategy based on stream data processing to reduce intra-core and inter-core communication latency. Develops weight mapping strategy to maximize crossbar array utilization for CNN deployment. Applies stream-based processing to schedule data flows and reduce handoffs between cores.

title: 8.7 A Dual VDD-Temperature Sensor Employing Sensor Fusion with 2.4°C, 9mV (±3σ) Inaccuracy in 65nm CMOS
problem: Heterogeneous 3D chiplet systems face acute thermal and power delivery challenges: thermal hotspots from high power density and workload-dependent supply voltage (VDD) gradients require fine-grained spatiotemporal monitoring via temperature and VDD sensors, but achieving high accuracy without external references is difficult.
method: Dual-sensor design combining temperature and VDD measurement via sensor fusion in 65nm CMOS; achieves 2.4°C and 9mV (±3σ) inaccuracy without external references, operating reliably despite VDD scaling and noise across different SoC domains.

title: GLOVA: Global and Local Variation-Aware Analog Circuit Design with Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning
problem: Analog/mixed-signal circuit design faces significant performance degradation from process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations and manufacturing mismatches, requiring iterative manual revisions and extensive simulations to achieve commercial-grade reliability.
method: GLOVA uses risk-sensitive reinforcement learning with ensemble-based critic to optimize analog circuit sizing while accounting for PVT variations and random mismatches. The framework employs mu-sigma evaluation and simulation reordering to reduce verification costs, supporting corner simulation and Monte Carlo methods for industrial-level validation.

title: Towards Training Robustness Against Dynamic Errors in Quantum Machine Learning
problem: Quantum machine learning training assumes static error rates in QNNs, but quantum noise is dynamic across time and qubits, causing performance degradation even when aggregate error rates appear similar.
method: A novel noise-aware training strategy dynamically adjusts to standard and fatal error conditions during QNN optimization, incorporating low-complexity fatal-error detection to identify problematic error patterns and adapt training accordingly.

title: Computational Advantage in Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks: Myth or Reality?
problem: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks (HQNNs) are proposed for enhanced computational performance, but it is unclear whether quantum layers provide genuine computational advantage over classical models when both scale to handle increasing problem complexity.
method: Comprehensive benchmarking of classical networks at increasing problem complexity identifies efficiency-optimal baselines. HQNNs (simulated on classical hardware) are systematically compared by measuring FLOP scaling and parameter growth rates as problem complexity increases (10 to 110 features), revealing architectural scaling efficiency differences.

title: Make Updates Faster: A Fast Multi-Stripe Updates Framework in Erasure-Coded Storage Clusters
problem: Erasure coding introduces high update penalties due to read-modify-write overhead; existing schemes don't fully exploit locality or adapt to heterogeneous network conditions.
method: Three-part framework: (1) Locality-aware update merging reduces network traffic by coalescing requests to same stripe, (2) Abstract update schemes into collector selection + tree construction, greedily balance load, (3) Dynamic scheduling adapts to heterogeneous network bandwidth.

title: 28.4 A 143dB-Dynamic-Range 119dB-CMRR Capacitance-to-Digital Converter for High-Resolution Floating-Target Displacement Sensing
problem: Capacitive displacement sensors for nanomechatronic systems are susceptible to high-frequency electric-field interference on electrically floating targets, requiring rejection of both low-frequency and high-frequency noise while maintaining high dynamic range (up to 500pF).
method: Phase-Domain-Delta-Sigma modulator (PD-ΔΣM) converts sensing capacitance to phase shift via lowpass RC front-end, then digitizes with high-resolution modulator. Inherent filtering in front-end/readout circuits provides dual-band noise rejection: 119dB CMRR near DC, 97dB around 100MHz, achieving 143dB dynamic range (35.2aF–500pF) without sub-ranging.

title: A 3x3.3mm Configurable Gamma Photon Spectrometer for Precision Radioguided Cancer Resection
problem: Radioguided surgery (RGS) for cancer removal requires gamma-sensing probes that can detect lesions at depth, differentiate lesion size/depth, and operate with high specificity; existing probes lack configurability, form-factor, and energy resolution.
method: A 180nm CMOS gamma spectrometer ASIC provides: (1) mm-scale pixelated design with single-gamma sensitivity, (2) per-pixel configurability for adaptive gain/threshold based on flux and PVT, (3) energy-resolving scheme with dynamic range to encode lesion depth via gamma energy profiles.
